name: register_service
description: Show an already running HTTP(S) service of a device in Workspace Services, for private Foundry-authenticated browser access. Name its exact loopback port; nothing is scanned or started. workspaceId is where it is listed, targetWorkspaceId the workspace on the device it runs on (default: workspaceId); the person must own that device. Reuse one registrationKey for retries. Closing access never stops the process. The status is reachability, not an application health check.
summary: Registers a known local web endpoint without starting or stopping it.
limits: Only the person's own executing devices and reachable workspaces, outside Issue-scoped sessions.
Only explicit loopback HTTP(S) ports; no arbitrary hosts or control ports.
Never public anonymous access; default private, sharing only from Foundry Web.

name: list_workspaces
description: List the workspaces you reach: id, name, device, your role. "unavailable" means its device no longer serves the folder. A session started in a workspace runs on its device, under that device's logins.
summary: Lists the workspaces the agent can reach, with each one's device and the agent's access there.
limits: Every workspace of the person who started the session, as at most Member.
A session working in an Issue reaches only the Issue's workspace.

name: list_resources
description: List what the devices you reach offer sessions and whether they are online: per device, its instances (browsers, macOS screen control, simulators, phones, GPUs, toolchains, accounts, disk, and compute) with type, state, why one is not ready and who leases it (detailed adds the rest). A computer_use instance with cua-driver, or a compute instance, can be leased with acquire_resource and used with operate_resource; compute runs commands there unless its owner turned that off. For anything else on a device, start a session in one of its workspaces.
summary: Shows what each reachable device offers sessions (browsers, screen control, simulators, GPUs, toolchains and more) with readiness, whether it is online and where a session may start on it.
limits: Only devices hosting a workspace the agent reaches.
Lists the device's own software; nothing is installed for the agent.
Readiness comes from detection on the device, never from a real use.

kind.description: Older filter of the per-device resources list; prefer type.

detailed.description: Also each instance's backends, details (CPUs, memory, versions), operations and last seen.

name: acquire_resource
description: Lease a resource on one of your person's devices for operate_resource: a Mac's screen (computer_use) or a device's compute. Name resourceId, several resourceIds (all or none), or a type and optionally deviceId. The lease lasts while your turn runs; when it ends it is parked up to 10 minutes (holdFor: up to 2 hours) and handed to a session that asks. A waiting session takes it 15 minutes after it began waiting; tool results warn you. Busy: waitMs queues up to that long, else you are told who holds it. Release it when done.
summary: Leases a resource on one of the person's devices (today a Mac's screen through cua-driver) to this session, waiting in a queue when it is busy.
limits: Only resources on devices the session's person owns; not from a session working in an Issue.
compute only on devices where "Allow remote commands from my sessions" is on (the default; the owner can turn it off on the Resources page).
Waits at most 10 minutes per call; a session holding a lease cannot wait for another.
At most 8 resources in one call, all or none.
Kept while the turn runs; afterwards parked at most 10 minutes, or holdFor at most 2 hours; taken 15 minutes after another session starts waiting.
The person can release any lease at any time.

resourceIds.description: Several resources to lease all at once, or none.

type.description: Without resourceId: lease the first ready resource of this type (default computer_use).

deviceId.description: With type: only on this device.

reason.description: What it is for, in a few words; the person sees it in the macOS notification and on the Resources page.

waitMs.description: How long to queue when it is busy, at most 600000; default 0 answers at once.

holdFor.description: Seconds to keep it parked after your turn ends (at most 7200); 0 removes the hold.

name: operate_resource
description: Run one operation, or a short batch in order (stopping at the first failure), on a resource you lease. A Mac's screen: select_window binds a window (pid + window_id) to the lease; the other operations are cua-driver's (screenshot, get_ui_tree, find_elements, list_apps, list_windows, open_app, activate_window, click, double_click, right_click, type_text, key, hotkey, scroll, drag, set_value, screen_size, wait). Prefer element_token from get_ui_tree to pixels; pixels refer to the window's latest screenshot through this lease (frame_id). Input goes in the background by default, best effort; foreground input and activate_window need delivery_mode: foreground, which needs the person's permission. A device's compute: run, put_files, get_file, git_sync, cleanup, as the worker's user in a named scratch folder that persists across leases, or in a workspace with workspaceId; a run answers exitCode, timedOut, durationMs and the tails of stdout and stderr. Each result says ok or an errorCode (stale_lease, stale_frame, backend_error).
summary: Operates a leased resource step by step: screenshots, accessibility tree, clicks, typing, keys, scrolling and dragging on a Mac's screen through cua-driver.
limits: Only with a live lease this session holds; refused once it ended or was taken.
At most 10 actions per call, run in order on the device; at most 120 seconds per call on a screen.

compute: a run blocks at most timeoutSec (default 600, at most 1800) and answers at most 128 KB of each stream's tail; put_files takes 50 MB in pieces of at most 768 KB of base64; get_file answers at most 25 MB per call; nothing outside the scratch folder or the named workspace.
Screenshots at most 1280 px on the long edge and 2 MB each, 8 MB per call; none are kept.
Every operation is audited for the person (typed text as its length only; a command line in full, env as its names, never output).

args.description: The operation's arguments, with cua-driver's own names. Windows are addressed by pid and window_id (from list_windows). select_window {pid, window_id}: bind this lease to a live window without activating it (read its UI tree); screenshot {pid?, window_id?, scope?: desktop, max_image_dimension? (at most 1280)}: one window (selected or with pid and window_id); the whole display requires explicit scope:desktop and no selection; get_ui_tree {pid, window_id, query?, max_elements?, max_depth?, include_screenshot?}: the accessibility tree with element_token per element; find_elements {pid, window_id, query}; list_apps {}; list_windows {pid?, on_screen_only?}; open_app {bundle_id | name, urls?}; activate_window {pid?, window_id?, delivery_mode: foreground} (brings it to the front, taking focus); click / double_click / right_click {element_token | x, y, pid?, window_id?, button?, count?, modifier?}; type_text {text, element_token?, pid?, window_id?} (does not press Return); key {key, modifiers?, pid?, window_id?}; hotkey {keys: ["cmd", "c"], pid?, window_id?}; scroll {direction, amount?, by?, element_token? | x, y, pid?, window_id?}; drag {from_x, from_y, to_x, to_y, pid?, window_id?, frame_id?, delivery_mode?} (background by default; unsupported background drag is refused); set_value {value, element_token, pid?, window_id?}; screen_size {}; wait {ms} (at most 5000). Input tools except set_value accept delivery_mode: background|foreground (default background); frame_id binds selected-window pixel input to the last capture. Omitted pid/window_id use the selected window, otherwise input needs an exact window pair or element_token. x and y are pixels in that window's latest screenshot taken through this lease; the backend maps them to the screen. compute (every operation takes scratch? (a folder name, default "default") or workspaceId?; paths are relative to it and cannot leave it): run {argv: ["pnpm", "test"] | command: "shell line", cwd?, env? {NAME: value}, timeoutSec? (default 600, at most 1800), tailBytes? (each stream, default 32768, at most 131072), saveOutput? (a file to write the whole output to)}; put_files {upload (a name you choose), offset (bytes already sent), data (base64 of the next piece), done? (true with the last piece), format? (tar | tar.gz | zip | file; default tar), dest? (folder to unpack into, or for file the file's path)}; get_file {path, offset?, length?}; git_sync {url (https), ref? (branch, tag or commit), dir? (default "repo")}: clones or fetches and checks out ref, keeping ignored files such as node_modules; cleanup {path?}: deletes the scratch folder, or a path in it.

actions.description: Several operations run in order, stopping at the first failure (after op, when both are given).

screenshotAfter.description: Also take a screenshot after the actions (of the window the last action named by pid and window_id, else the selected window; without selection explicitly request scope:desktop).

name: release_resource
description: Release a lease you hold: the device resets the resource and gives it to the next session waiting.
summary: Releases a lease this session holds so the next session can use the resource.
limits: Only the session holding the lease; the person releases any lease on the Resources page.

name: resource_status
description: Read one resource (resourceId) or your lease (leaseId): state, readiness, holder, queue, your lease's deadlines and its latest operations.
summary: Shows a resource's state, holder, queue, the session's own lease on it and its latest operations.
limits: Only resources on devices the session's person owns.
The latest 10 operations, as audited (typed text as its length only).

name: list_profiles
description: List the agent profiles (accounts and model endpoints) of a device you reach: id, runtime, model, status; your device by default. A compatible endpoint shows its baseUrl and models, never its key.
summary: Lists the agent profiles and assigned model services (runtime, endpoint, models, status) on one device.
limits: The calling session's device, or another device hosting a workspace the agent reaches.

deviceId.description: Device that owns the profiles; defaults to the calling device.

name: list_models
description: List the models a profile can run, on your device by default or another you reach.
summary: Lists the models a profile can run, from its endpoint's catalog.
limits: The calling session's device, or another device hosting a workspace the agent reaches.

deviceId.description: Device that owns the profiles; defaults to the calling device.

name: create_session
description: Start a new Foundry session: a separate chat whose first message is prompt. By default it runs in your workspace on your device and, without profileId or provider, like you; with workspaceId, in another workspace you reach as Member, on that workspace's device, as its default agent or else an account that works there (none usable: refused with no_usable_account and the device's accounts). An offline device queues it (waitingForDevice) until it is back, and it fails after 24 h offline. It works in the workspace folder itself, not a copy. At most 8 of your sessions queued, running or blocked at once, and 4 levels of nesting. Each turn it ends is reported to your inbox as a turn_end message (title, status, the first 1500 characters of its answer, a link) that starts your next turn; reportBack: false turns this off. Answers with the new session's id and status.
summary: Starts a separate conversation for cross-domain or independently tracked work, including an independent verifier; prefer native subagents for temporary local parts.
limits: At most 8 sessions it started queued, running or blocked at once.
Sessions that start sessions nest at most 4 levels below the first one.
Needs Member in the target workspace; the session runs on that workspace's device, under its logins.
At most 10 attachments, each at most 25 MB, from the caller's own workspace folder.
A verifier runs in the read-only verification sandbox: the workspace is read-only at the operating-system level, it writes only to its temporary directory, and its Foundry tools only read.

title.description: Short title for the chat list, in the person's language; default: the start of the prompt.

attachments.description: Files to copy to the session: paths in your workspace folder or att_… ids you were given; at most 10, 25 MB each. They land in one folder under .foundry/attachments of its workspace (deliveredAttachments lists the paths); a session on another device sees only files handed over this way.

verification.description: Start a read-only verifier: the workspace is read-only for it and every command it runs (tests, linters and git work; writes fail), it writes only to its temporary directory and gets only the Foundry tools that read. Needs a current worker.

forkSessionId.description: Start from a copy of this session's native transcript (the source is untouched), in its workspace; needs Member there.

issueId.description: Run in that Issue's candidate worktree and sandbox; the Issue must be in this workspace and in progress, blocked or verifying.

reportBack.description: Default true. false: no turn_end reports; read its results with get_session.

workspaceId.description: Workspace to start it in, one you reach as Member; default: yours.

name: list_sessions
description: List a workspace's sessions, newest activity first, one line each (id, title, status, runtime, profile, device, parent, activity). Yours by default, or workspaceId; parentSessionId lists the sessions one session started; parentOnly the ones you started. Pages of limit with the nextCursor a page returns.
summary: Lists a workspace's sessions, newest activity first, one line each.
limits: Pages of at most 100 sessions, 30 by default.

workspaceId.description: Workspace to list; defaults to yours with a session token.

parentOnly.description: Only the sessions your session created (needs a session token).

parentSessionId.description: Only the sessions this session (an id or a Foundry chat link) started.

limit.description: Sessions per page; default 30, at most 100.

cursor.description: The nextCursor of the previous page.

name: list_group_sessions
description: List one orchestration group's sessions in list order, in list_sessions' form; read_context's summary names a session's group.
summary: Lists the sessions of one orchestration group in list order.
limits: Only groups in workspaces the agent reaches.

workspaceId.description: The group's workspace; defaults to yours with a session token.

name: get_session
description: A session's or native chat's summary: the same as read_context scope=summary.
summary: Reads one session's or native chat's summary: status, runtime, lineage, last input and answer, last error.
limits: The last input is cut to 300 characters and the answer to 1000.

sessionId.description: A session id (sess_…), a native chat id (native_claude_…, native_codex_…) or a Foundry chat link.

name: read_context
description: Read a session or native chat you can read, in any workspace you reach. scope: summary (default: status, places, lineage, last input and answer, open work, last error); events (one line each; filter by levels, labels, query; the newest with tail, or pages of limit with after/before cursors; labels ["User message"] lists the person's own messages); thread (the conversation: messages and answers without tool calls; the newest page, or from offset; at most limit messages, each cut at maxChars; transcript is the same for a native chat); changes (the files it wrote or named, with lines added and removed; with path, that file's diff, one turn's with inputId); file (path: the file as it is now on the session's device); background (commands it left running; taskId: the end of one's output); subagents (its native subagents; taskId: one's transcript). file and a diff are read in lines: from offset, at most limit. Every answer stays within maxBytes and says how to read on.
summary: Reads a session in depth: its events, transcript, native subagents, the files it changed and the commands it left running.
limits: Output is cut at maxBytes, 12000 by default.
Pages of at most 500 events, with up to 5 events of context each.
A background command's output needs Member in the session's workspace.

sessionId.description: A session id (sess_…), a native chat id (native_claude_…, native_codex_…) or a Foundry chat link.

query.description: events: only events containing this text.

tail.description: events: the last N matches (at most 500).

limit.description: Page size: events (default 50, at most 500), thread messages (default 20, at most 200), file or diff lines (default 400, at most 2000).

after.description: events: only after this cursor (an event id it printed, or a time).

context.description: events: also up to N events (at most 5) before each match.

taskId.description: subagents: the subagent; background: the task.

path.description: changes: the file whose diff to read; file: the file to read.

inputId.description: changes with path: only that turn.

offset.description: Where a page starts: thread, the message index (from 0); file or diff, the line (from 1). Without it thread reads the newest page.

maxChars.description: thread: cut each message to this many characters (default 2000); chars gives the whole length.

name: list_issues
description: List a workspace's Issues, newest update first, one line each: id, title, status, contract, latest run, waiting question, criteria verified. Yours by default, or workspaceId; in an Issue, only it. Read-only: the person drives Issues.
summary: Lists a workspace's Issues with their status, contract, latest run and verification progress.
limits: Read-only: the person drives Issues in Foundry.
A session working in an Issue sees only that Issue.

workspaceId.description: Workspace to list; defaults to yours with a session token.

name: get_issue
description: Read one Issue: status, the person's request, the confirmed contract and each criterion's latest verdict, any newer draft, the question waiting for the person, the verification summary and its latest run (session id, status, error).
summary: Reads one Issue: the request, the confirmed contract with each criterion's verdict, the waiting question and the latest run.
limits: Read-only: the person drives Issues in Foundry.
A session working in an Issue sees only that Issue.

issueId.description: The Issue's id (iss_…) or short id.

name: send_message
description: Send a message to a session you control: one your person or their agents started, in a workspace you reach as Member (in an Issue, only its sessions; never an Issue's own execution or clarification). An idle session takes it as its next turn; profileId, provider or model switch its runtime first. A running session is steered according to delivery: boundary (default) at its next step (Claude between tool rounds, Codex while a tool runs, within 15 minutes); interrupt at once (Claude after its running tool calls; at most 2 per sender per 30 minutes); turn_end when its turn ends or after 10 minutes. A queued, finishing or offline session holds the message (waitingForDevice) and several held messages start one turn. Messages from sessions are never dropped; the same inputId, or the same text to the same session within 10 minutes, is the earlier message. Only sessions you created report their turns to you: ask any other to send you its result. Answers with the session's status and the message's receipt (inputId, delivery, state, deliverAt).
summary: Messages a session: steers a running one or continues an idle one, and can switch its runtime first.
limits: Only sessions the person or their agents started, in workspaces reached as Member; in an Issue, only the Issue's sessions.
Never an Issue's execution or clarification: their Issue drives them.
The runtime switches only while the session is idle.
At most 10 attachments, each at most 25 MB, from the caller's own workspace folder.

sessionId.description: A session id (sess_…), a native chat id (native_claude_…, native_codex_…) or a Foundry chat link.

delivery.description: boundary (default), interrupt or turn_end, as described above; ignored for a person's message.

inputId.description: Your own lowercase UUID for the message: sending it again returns the first receipt.

attachments.description: Files to copy to the session: paths in your workspace folder or att_… ids you were given; at most 10, 25 MB each. They land in one folder under .foundry/attachments of its workspace (deliveredAttachments lists the paths); a session on another device sees only files handed over this way.

name: cancel_session
description: Stop the current work of a session you control. Sessions it started keep running; send_message continues it later.
summary: Stops the work a session is doing; the session stays usable.
limits: Only sessions the person or their agents started, in workspaces reached as Member; in an Issue, only the Issue's sessions.
Never cascades: the sessions it started keep running.

sessionId.description: A session id (sess_…), a native chat id (native_claude_…, native_codex_…) or a Foundry chat link.

name: rename_session
description: Rename a session you control (1-120 characters).
summary: Renames a session.
limits: Only sessions the person or their agents started, in workspaces reached as Member; in an Issue, only the Issue's sessions.
Titles of 1–120 characters.

sessionId.description: An id (sess_…) or a Foundry chat link.

name: ask_person
description: Ask the person something only they can decide (a choice the confirmed contract leaves open) or allow (a side effect outside the candidate, such as deploying or sending a message). Only an Issue's execution has this tool. After calling it, end your turn with a short summary of where you are; the Issue waits for the person and Foundry resumes you in the same candidate with their answer. Ask one question at a time and never about anything you can decide yourself.
summary: Asks the person what only they can decide or allow; the Issue waits for the answer and Foundry resumes the session with it.
limits: Only an Issue's execution has it.
Questions of up to 4000 bytes, with up to 6 suggested answers.

question.description: What you need, in the person's language, with the context they need to answer.

kind.description: input: a decision or information; permission: approval for a specific action. Defaults to input.

options.description: Up to 6 suggested answers; the person may answer otherwise.

name: feishu_events
description: Receive the events (messages, card actions, approvals) of a Feishu app your person connected in Connectors. Without subscriptionId it subscribes and buffers from then on; with it, it returns what arrived since the last call (waiting up to timeoutMs for the first), in order with a cursor each, and acknowledges the previous answer; pass a cursor to read one again. Unsubscribe when done. Reply as the bot with feishu-cli.
summary: Subscribes to a connected Feishu app's events and returns them by cursor, waiting for the next.
limits: Only apps the session's person connected in Connectors.
At most 8 subscriptions per session, each buffering at most 500 unread events; beyond that the oldest are dropped and counted.
At most 100 events per call; waits at most 10 minutes per call.
A subscription nobody calls for 30 minutes ends.

subscriptionId.description: The subscription to read (fsub_…); omit to subscribe.

appId.description: When subscribing: the Feishu app id (cli_…) or Connectors app id (xapp_…); optional with one connected app.

eventTypes.description: When subscribing: event types to keep, e.g. ["im.message.receive_v1"]; default every type.

chatId.description: When subscribing: keep only events in this chat (oc_…).

cursor.description: Return events after this cursor; default after the last call's answer.

maxEvents.description: At most this many events, up to 100 (default 50). more: true says others are waiting.

timeoutMs.description: How long to wait for the first event, at most 600000; default 0 when subscribing, 60000 when reading.

unsubscribe.description: End the subscription named by subscriptionId.

name: find_workspace
description: Find the projects (workspaces) a request belongs in, best first, matched on name, summary, routing notes, your note cards/<workspaceId>.md and recent activity. Each candidate has why it matched, a score (only order and gaps mean anything) and stale (call get_workspace before acting there); close says the top two are a tie. Pass the request in the person's words. Archived projects are left out.
summary: Ranks the person's projects for a request, with why each matched and how fresh its summary is.
limits: At most 5 candidates per call.
Only projects the person can read; archived ones are left out.
Only the person's assistant (a personal_agent session) has it.

query.description: The request, in the person's own words.

name: get_workspace
description: Read one project: its summary (purpose, routing notes, latest sessions, open Issues, skills, connectors, Git branch) and accounts (which can run a session there and why not, defaultProfileId, defaultAgent); include adds live state (device online, running sessions, Git), instructions (the start of AGENTS.md or README) and your note.
summary: Reads one project's summary, live state, instructions and the assistant's routing note.
limits: Only projects the person can read.
Live checks need the project's device online; otherwise they say it is offline.
The instructions excerpt is at most 8 KiB.
Only the person's assistant (a personal_agent session) has it.

workspaceId.description: The project's id (ws_…), from find_workspace or list_workspaces.

include.description: What to read besides the summary; all three by default.

name: create_workspace
description: Create a project with its own files: a short human name, a one-sentence purpose and the skills it needs. source.kind: empty (a new folder), clone (source.url) or existing (source.path, a folder the person has). needs lists what it needs from a computer, as the key:value words your snapshot lists; without deviceId Foundry picks a device that has them. Answers the project (id, name, device) and why that place, or {"status": "no_place_fits", "missing", "computers"} when none fits. The answer may instead be {"status": "needs_confirmation", "proposalId", "summary"}: a card is in front of the person and Foundry tells you their answer. A "not allowed" error is final.
summary: Creates and registers a new project (empty, cloned or an existing folder), or proposes it to the person.
limits: Only on the person's own devices that allow new projects, inside their managed folders (default ~/Foundry).
Never on a device whose system account other people's devices share.
At most 3 new projects a day and 10 a week by default (at most 10 and 30).
Registering a folder outside the managed folders asks the person first by default.
Only the person's assistant (a personal_agent session) has it.

name.description: A short human name, 1-80 characters; the folder is named after it.

purpose.description: One sentence: what the project is for. It feeds the project's summary.

gitInit.description: Only for a new empty engineering workspace that needs Git; default false.

path.description: The folder to register (kind existing), absolute on the device.

skills.description: Skills to add, by name: the person's own or Foundry's built-in ones.

needs.description: What the work cannot do without, as words from the snapshot ("network:corp", "reaches:<host>", "toolchain:go", "files:work", "gpu", "always-on"); empty for self-contained work.

deviceId.description: The device (dev_…) the person named; omit to let Foundry choose by needs.

name: update_workspace
description: Change a project the person owns: rename it, restate its purpose, add or remove skills, and add or remove the person's connector accounts (connectors.add lets its sessions act as the person outside Foundry). Answers the project before and after. The answer may instead be {"status": "needs_confirmation", "proposalId", "summary"}: a card is in front of the person and Foundry tells you their answer. A "not allowed" error is final.
summary: Renames a project, restates its purpose, or changes its skills and connector accounts, or proposes it.
limits: Only projects the person owns, on devices the person owns.
Binding an account to a project asks the person the first time by default.
Removing a skill from a project the assistant did not create asks first by default.
Only the person's assistant (a personal_agent session) has it.

add.description: The person's connector account ids to bind.

name: archive_workspace
description: Archive a project (hidden, starts no sessions, nothing deleted), or restore it with restore=true. Projects cannot be deleted. The answer may instead be {"status": "needs_confirmation", "proposalId", "summary"}: a card is in front of the person and Foundry tells you their answer. A "not allowed" error is final.
summary: Archives a finished project, keeping everything, or restores an archived one.
limits: Only projects the person owns.
Nothing is deleted: files, sessions and history stay.
Archiving asks the person first by default; restoring does not.
Only the person's assistant (a personal_agent session) has it.

restore.description: Bring an archived project back instead.

name: remember
description: Keep, correct or forget one durable fact about the person. op add stores item.content; update replaces item.id's content (the old one is kept as superseded); forget erases item.id. add and update need item.quote, the person's own words from this conversation; a fact whose quote is not found waits for the person to confirm it in settings. item.inferred marks a fact you concluded (no quote). With a Memory Workspace selected, confirmed facts are queued to its owner files (give intentKey and title).
summary: Stores, corrects or forgets one fact about the person, recording where it came from.
limits: One item per call, at most 300 characters.
A fact is the person's only when its quote is found in what they wrote in this conversation; otherwise it is a guess or waits for their confirmation.
The person sees, edits and forgets every item in settings.
Only the person's assistant (a personal_agent session) has it.

id.description: The item to update or forget.

content.description: The fact, one short sentence (add, update).

quote.description: The person's own words the fact rests on, copied from their messages in this conversation (… for words left out).

inferred.description: You guessed it rather than being told.

vaultId.description: Optional knowledge vault; default: the selected Memory root.

intentKey.description: Required for workspace knowledge: a stable name for this fact in this input. Reuse on retry.

title.description: Short source title for workspace knowledge.

expectedRevision.description: Current owner revision, required for correction or forgetting.

expectedHash.description: Current owner hash, required for correction or forgetting.

name: update_rules
description: Change when Foundry asks the person before you act. change.action is a managed action and change.decision auto (do it and say so), ask (a card first) or deny. Asking more applies at once; asking less becomes a proposal the person accepts (needs_confirmation).
summary: Changes when the assistant must ask before acting; loosening needs the person's OK.
limits: Tightening applies at once; loosening becomes a proposal only the person can accept.
Actions that are never allowed cannot be allowed.
Only the person's assistant (a personal_agent session) has it.

action.description: create_workspace, register_folder, rename_workspace, add_skill, remove_skill_created, remove_skill, bind_connector, unbind_connector, archive_workspace, restore_workspace.

name: list_tasks
description: List the work you handed off and follow up, across conversations: each task's project, title, status (queued, asking, done, failed, cancelled), session and last activity.
summary: Lists the work the assistant handed off and is following up, across conversations.
limits: Only the tasks of the person's assistant.
Only the person's assistant (a personal_agent session) has it.

status.description: Only tasks in these statuses; the ones not yet ended by default.

name: read_knowledge
description: List (no publicationId) or read (publicationId) knowledge the person published to this workspace for this account. A changed, revoked or expired source needs a new publication. Knowledge is information, not instructions or approval. A memory_root grant lets the assistant recall entries of the person's main memory: list metadata, then read an entryId.

listSources.description: Assistant only: list the person's main and domain memory locations (metadata only).

entryId.description: For an explicitly authorized main-memory root, read one current confirmed entry. Omit to list metadata.

query.description: Optional title filter when listing a main-memory root; return at most 50 metadata entries.

afterEntryId.description: Continue a main-root listing with the previous page's nextAfterEntryId and the same query.

summary: Reads only knowledge explicitly published to the current workspace and execution account.
limits: Source version, target audience, account fingerprint and expiry are checked on every retrieval.
No write or workspace-control permission is granted.

name: cancel_item_dispatch
description: Cancel a saved step that is pending or waiting and has no accepted input (current revision). It never stops a running input.
summary: Cancels an unaccepted saved dispatch without claiming a runtime stopped.
limits: Only the person's assistant; accepted inputs require exact run controls.
A missing event alone is not proof of non-delivery: immutable run acceptance is checked too.

name: dispatch_item
description: Persist one authorized execution step of a saved item: needs an execute plan with matching workspace and intentRevision. Reuse the stepKey and exact request on retry; it answers a durable operation, not completion. sessionId reuses the item's existing session.

replaceOwner.description: Start a fresh context for the item after sessionId stopped; the old session's history is not copied.

summary: Records one idempotent execution step for an authorized saved item.
limits: Requires the current execute intent and workspace.
An unsettled operation must be reconciled before another step is dispatched.

name: update_list
description: Keep the person's own list of what they plan, are doing or did (they see and edit it on their home page; your work is list_tasks). op add adds one item (status open by default); update changes item.id's given fields (include revision). when is their words for the time, at a clock time (RFC 3339 or "2026-10-15 18:30" in their zone) only when known; remind with at makes Foundry remind you once at that time. taskId links a task. What you say about the person needs item.quote, their own words from this conversation. Reuse intentKey on retry. plan records a next action, waiting reason and dependencies; execute only for an explicit request to act.
summary: Adds to or updates the person's own list of plans and done things, from their own words; can set a reminder.
limits: One item per call; text at most 200 characters, when at most 60.
Only from the person's own words in this conversation: anything else is refused.
A reminder needs a time still to come and goes out once, unless the assistant is stopped.
The person ticks, edits and deletes items on the assistant's home page.
Only the person's assistant (a personal_agent session) has it.

text.description: The thing, one short line in the person's language ("Reply to the recruiters on WeChat").

when.description: When, in the person's words; empty when they did not say.

at.description: when as a time: RFC 3339, or "2026-10-15 18:30" in their time zone; empty clears it.

remind.description: Foundry reminds you at at while the item is open; needs at.

status.description: open (to do or doing), done, or dropped (they will not do it).

taskId.description: Your task helping with it (list_tasks); empty unlinks.

quote.description: The person's own words this rests on, from this conversation (… for words left out); not needed to change only taskId.

revision.description: Current item revision from read_list; a stale update is refused. Pass it when updating.

intentKey.description: Stable key for this intent within the current input; reuse it on retries.

mode.description: record unless the person asked you to execute; this field alone grants no permission.

name: read_list
description: Read the person's list: the open items and those done or dropped since closedSince (default: the start of their today), with the time now in their zone.
summary: Reads the person's own list of plans and done things.
limits: Only the list of the assistant's own person.
Only the person's assistant (a personal_agent session) has it.

closedSince.description: Also items closed since this date (2026-10-13, in the person's time zone) or time (RFC 3339).

name: list_session_work
description: List persistent work: schedules, background processes and subagents of this conversation (or sessionId), earlier turns included, with unconfirmed controls. workspaceId lists a workspace's persistent services instead. With id: that item and its run history.
summary: Lists persistent schedules, background commands and subagents across the conversation, including pending controls.

workspaceId.description: List this workspace's persistent services instead.

sessionId.description: Defaults to the calling session; reads and controls its whole conversation work inventory.

id.description: Work ID; includes durable run history when provided.

limits: Uses the existing session and workspace access rules; inspecting commands requires control permission for the target session.
Device observation and control require an updated worker. A pending or unknown receipt does not prove execution has stopped.

name: control_session_work
description: Control persistent work: stop, pause (no future runs), resume, run a schedule now, stop_all (this conversation's work, not shared services, native subagents or child sessions), or link/unlink a session to a shared service. Single actions need the item's current revision; reuse idempotencyKey for retries. A control is done only when list_session_work shows the device confirmed it.
summary: Pauses, resumes or stops conversation work, returning a durable receipt that devices must confirm.

sessionId.description: Defaults to the calling session; reads and controls its whole conversation work inventory.

expectedReferenceRevision.description: A shared service's referenceRevision from the latest list; required after its links changed.

relatedSessionId.description: link/unlink: the session to associate; this never starts or stops the process.

limits: Uses the existing session and workspace access rules; inspecting commands requires control permission for the target session.
Device observation and control require an updated worker. A pending or unknown receipt does not prove execution has stopped.
Unassigned OS sources require explicit association by the person. Disabling host cron does not prove its earlier external executions have stopped.

name: create_scheduled_work
description: Create a wake-up (kind=schedule) or a persistent local service (kind=process) that outlives the agent's own process; for timers and background commands within the session, use your own tools. A schedule takes cron with an IANA timeZone, or at (an RFC3339 instant). Reusing idempotencyKey returns the same work.
summary: Creates durable wake-ups or persistent local services; ordinary background tasks use native tools.

sessionId.description: Defaults to the calling session; reads and controls its whole conversation work inventory.

limits: Uses the existing session and workspace access rules; inspecting commands requires control permission for the target session.
Device observation and control require an updated worker. A pending or unknown receipt does not prove execution has stopped.

name: refresh_workspace_skills
description: Refresh this workspace's draft skills from .agents/skills: returns immutable snapshot paths and digests you can read and trial in this turn. It does not register them as native skills or publish them.
summary: Discover and snapshot the current workspace’s Skill drafts for trial.
limits: Only the caller’s own workspace execution root; no arbitrary device paths.
Requires a connected worker supporting workspace drafts and enabled workspace draft settings.

name: cloudflare
description: Work with the Cloudflare zones the person bound to this session's workspace, through the official Cloudflare MCP and Foundry's gateway; credentials stay on the server. Start with action accounts: it lists the eligible Cloudflare identities, their bound zone IDs, granted permissions and the workspace's access level. Then action request with accountId, method (default GET), path and, for a change, body. Access levels, which the person sets per workspace in Connectors → Cloudflare (Workspace access): read allows GET of /zones (the bound zones), /zones/<id>, its DNS records (/zones/<id>/dns_records[/<record id>], with query name, type, match, page, per_page, order, direction) and SSL/certificate metadata; DNS edit adds POST /zones/<id>/dns_records (create: body {type, name, content, ttl, proxied, comment}), PATCH or PUT /zones/<id>/dns_records/<record id> (update) and DELETE /zones/<id>/dns_records/<record id>, for example A records or ACME DNS-01 _acme-challenge TXT records. Every change goes to the account's activity log the person sees in Connectors. A request outside the workspace's level is refused with the level that would allow it; then ask the person to choose it there, or to re-authorize the account if its permissions lack dns.write. Unbinding or disconnecting ends access at once.
summary: Reads the bound Cloudflare zones, DNS and certificate metadata, and changes DNS records where the workspace has DNS edit access.
limits: Requires the account owner’s active session on their own device and an explicit workspace zone binding.
Changes need the DNS edit access level, which the person grants per workspace; they cover DNS records of the bound zones only and are logged on the account.

accountId.description: Foundry connected-account id from action accounts; not the Cloudflare account or zone id.

method.description: Default GET. POST, PATCH, PUT and DELETE change DNS records and need the DNS edit access level.

path.description: Cloudflare API path without /client/v4, e.g. /zones/<zone id>/dns_records.

body.description: JSON body of a POST, PATCH or PUT: the DNS record fields.

name: archive_session
description: Archive sessions or a chat folder, or restore them with restore=true. Archived chats stay readable; messages to them fail until restored, and their scheduled work pauses (restoring does not resume it). Running, queued, Issue-owned and assistant home sessions cannot be archived. Agents archive their person's sessions and, outside an Issue, native chats of a workspace on a device their person paired. The person's assistant asks first for folders or more than 3 chats.
summary: Archive and restore sessions
limits: Only sessions you control; explicit restore required before sending.
